OpenMP/BLAS thread-count guard: sets OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL/VECLIB/NUMEXPR thread env vars from a small named profile (serial/balanced/perf/...) as early as Python startup allows, so multiple native math runtimes loaded by different dependencies don't each grab all cores and thrash. Pure stdlib, no product imports

fail-closed retention policy for immutable dashboard/console release builds: distinguishes complete vs. partial (in-progress) release directories by an exact filename-identity regex, enforces a minimum age before a partial can be reclaimed, and keeps at least N unreferenced complete releases so a rollback target always exists. Stdlib + fcntl only

the single reviewed allowlist (Finder metadata + bytecode cache only) shared by both release construction and startup verification, plus a bounded-parallelism content-hash inventory of a release tree used to prove two builds are byte-identical. Stdlib only

captures an immutable boot identity (git commit/tree, captured-at, dirty-at-boot) once at process import time, so a long-running server process keeps naming the code generation it actually booted from even after the on-disk checkout advances underneath it, instead of laundering newer disk state as if it were live. Stdlib + subprocess only

The process-group launcher: forks a session-leader child that is held on a private pipe until a two-phase release-token handshake proves the sidecar/PGID receipt has converged, then execs the real command as pgid==pid so the whole tree is one killable group; on SIGTERM/SIGINT or parent loss it TERM-polls-KILLs the group before exiting. This is the 'process-group launch + content-addressed job identity' primitive named in the assignment. Renamed from a leading-underscore private script to a proper importable/executable module.

edits.reason: PRIVACY TRANSFORM: the on-disk PGID receipt must never carry the full command line, only opaque sha256 refs over it.
PRIVACY TRANSFORM: drop every absolute host path from the persisted receipt, keep only the file-identity hashes (opaque refs, no host paths).
drop the last remaining spread of raw absolute control-file paths into the receipt; the control directory is already reachable from job_id, no need to persist its resolved path.
these two locals only fed the now-removed canonical_coord_db_path/canonical_release_path receipt fields; dead after the privacy edits above.

files.reason: The simpler process-group launcher used for an exclusive-lane workload (Popen(start_new_session=True) is the macOS-safe way to get a fresh session/group leader without a bare os.setsid() EPERM). TERM-polls-KILL on signal, mirrors the real child's exit code (128+sig if signalled). Complements pglaunch.py as the lighter-weight variant with no two-phase custody handshake.

edits.reason: PRIVACY TRANSFORM: drop the absolute progress_file host path from the persisted PGID receipt; job/pgid/pid identity is all a caller needs.

files.reason: The memory admission gate: 'wait until N GB + a 6 GB safety buffer of headroom exists, polling every 30s' / 'check now' / 'print status'. Delegates its actual headroom read to lib_safety.sh's mem_free_gb so there is one source of truth. This is the 'resource-mode governor' primitive's admission half. Already fully generic — no product-specific vocabulary anywhere in the file, ported with no content edits.

Single-source-of-truth shared shell primitives: a stable memory_pressure-based free-RAM read (mem_free_gb) with a vm_stat fallback, swap/load reads, and safe process-group teardown for an exclusive-lane lock (gpu_pgid_is_ours proves a pgid is still the live, un-recycled group we launched before anyone signals it; kill_pgid_escalate is TERM->poll->KILL that refuses to ever signal its own process group and only returns success once the group is confirmed empty). This is the fcntl/PID-liveness-adjacent safety layer the assignment asks for, generalized from the specific 'GPU lane' framing to any exclusive lock directory holding a pgid.json sidecar.

files.reason: AST lint for the five silent-plausible-value defect shapes (P1-P5). Stdlib-only (ast/json/re/argparse), no product imports; every literal that names the source product lives in the module docstring or a code comment, both stripped automatically by the porter. Only the scan-root/allowlist path constants and one closing print message are live strings that need edits.

edits.reason: The source hardcoded a scan root nested under a fixed coordharness/src/coordharness tree and an allowlist path under coordharness/config/. The harness scans whatever project it is coordinating, so the scan root becomes the coordinated project's root (config.project_root()) and the allowlist moves into harness state (config.state_dir()), matching the pattern already used by every other ported module that needs a writable sidecar.

The source treated a missing allowlist as a hard operator error because the file was checked into the private repo's config/ directory in advance. In the harness the allowlist lives in generated state (.coordharness/), so first run must self-bootstrap an empty one rather than fail closed, mirroring the existing self-bootstrapping config pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase (docs_hygiene's CONFIG_PATH).

Live print statement (not a docstring/comment, so the porter's automatic strip does not touch it) that cited an internal work-item-ID'd report and a product-specific gate script by name. Replaced with a generic pointer to the allowlist/ratchet mechanism that ships in this repo instead.

files.reason: AST lint flagging relative-string-literal path arguments to Path()/open()/pandas-style read_*()/sqlite3.connect()/duckdb.connect() -- the exact class of defect where a path resolves from the test-runner cwd but not the production process cwd. Stdlib-only, no product imports; same two-constant-block-plus-one-message shape as the fail-loud lint above.

edits.reason: Same rationale as the fail-loud lint's path block: scan the coordinated project, keep the reviewed-allowlist sidecar in harness state instead of a fixed product config directory.
Same self-bootstrap fix as the fail-loud lint: the allowlist is generated harness state, not a pre-populated checked-in file, so a missing file should seed empty rather than hard-fail.
Live print statement citing an internal work-item-ID'd report by name; replaced with a self-contained instruction that does not depend on the private repo's report archive.

files.reason: Read-only git-diff auditor: for every deleted or renamed file under a protected doc set, classifies the deletion as a safe archive move/copy, an unpreserved deletion, or a non-archive relocation needing review (byte-hash match, falling back to a line-similarity same-basename match at a 0.85 threshold for near-identical moves). Pure stdlib (subprocess/hashlib/difflib), fully generic mechanism -- only the protected-path convention was hardcoded to this product's doc tree.

edits.reason: The protected-doc convention (which root files, which archive prefix) was hardcoded to this product's three root ledgers and its coordharness/docs/ tree. Made configurable via env vars with generic defaults (docs/, docs/archive/, no hardcoded root filenames) so any project can point this at its own doc layout without editing code.

Live f-string-able message hardcoded the coordharness/docs/archive path; now reflects the configured ARCHIVE_PREFIX so the emitted JSON stays accurate for whatever archive convention the caller configured.

files.reason: Rewrites two generated, marker-delimited index blocks (a live-docs index and an archive-docs index) so every tracked Markdown file under docs/ is reachable from one of two indexes -- the anti-loss invariant that nothing gets silently orphaned by a move to archive/. Pure stdlib (re/pathlib), no product imports; only the docs-root resolution needs to point at the coordinated project instead of a fixed sibling directory.

edits.reason: The source resolved docs/ as a fixed sibling of the script (coordharness/docs), assuming the script always lives inside the tree it scans. The harness runs against an arbitrary coordinated project, so this resolves docs/ under that project's root instead.

files.reason: Intraprocedural AST taint lint: within each function it marks local variables assigned from a named 'unsafe provenance' producer call (fixpoint over three passes so `b = a or fallback` inherits a's taint), then flags any named sink-constructor call whose named keyword argument's expression mentions a tainted name. The taint-propagation mechanism is fully generic; only the specific producer/sink/owner names were this product's own class names (one of which is a business-specific metric name, replaced below). Ported as a working example with clearly-marked example config rather than a hardcoded fixture.

edits.reason: UI_ROOT assumed a fixed coordharness/src/coordharness/ui path; pointed at the coordinated project's src/ instead. FIG_OWNERS carried three of this product's own class names, one of which (a share-of-contested-matters metric class) names a business concept rather than a generic mechanism; dropped it and relabeled the remaining two as explicit example config so a reader understands these are meant to be replaced with their own project's class names, not treated as a real default.

The original computed a display path via root.parents[3], a magic index that only worked because UI_ROOT sat exactly four directories below the source repo's root (coordharness/src/coordharness/ui). That assumption breaks under the new UI_ROOT. Since every path came from root.rglob(...), it is always a descendant of root, so relative_to(root) is both correct and simpler -- not a cosmetic rename, a genuine fix for the changed root depth.
